title: The Historical Map with a Place Name That Later Changed
sentences: Students compared an old town map with a modern map while researching a former riverside factory.
The old map marked a place called Sakura Landing beside the river.
The modern map had no Sakura Landing, but it showed Sakura Park several hundred meters upstream.
Some students assumed the park had been built on the exact site of the old landing because the name was similar.
A city record explained that the landing closed in 1958 and that the park received the old district name when it opened in 1974.
The record included coordinates showing that the two sites were not the same.
Students returned to the old map and used a bridge that still existed as a fixed reference point.
That placed the former landing downstream from the modern park, near what is now a parking area.
The project labeled the two sites separately and explained why the shared name could be misleading.
Students also avoided saying the parking area itself had existed when the landing was active.
Their final map used dates and a surviving landmark to connect old and modern geography accurately.
They learned that a place name can move or be reused, so matching names alone does not prove matching locations.

slashRows.en: Students compared an old town map with a modern map while researching a former riverside factory.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは川沿いの旧工場を調べるため古い町地図と現在の地図を比べました。

slashRows.en: The old map marked a place called Sakura Landing beside the river.
slashRows.jp: 古い地図には川のそばに「桜船着場」という場所がありました。

slashRows.en: The modern map had no Sakura Landing, but it showed Sakura Park several hundred meters upstream.
slashRows.jp: 現在の地図には船着場はなく、数百メートル上流に桜公園がありました。

slashRows.en: Some students assumed the park had been built on the exact site of the old landing because the name was similar.
slashRows.jp: 名前が似ているため、公園が旧船着場と全く同じ場所だと考える生徒もいました。

slashRows.en: A city record explained that the landing closed in 1958 and that the park received the old district name when it opened in 1974.
slashRows.jp: 市の記録では船着場は一九五八年閉鎖、公園は一九七四年開園時に旧地区名を受け継いだとありました。

slashRows.en: The record included coordinates showing that the two sites were not the same.
slashRows.jp: 記録の位置情報から二つの場所は同じではないと分かりました。

slashRows.en: Students returned to the old map and used a bridge that still existed as a fixed reference point.
slashRows.jp: 生徒は古地図へ戻り、今もある橋を固定した基準点として使いました。

slashRows.en: That placed the former landing downstream from the modern park, near what is now a parking area.
slashRows.jp: その結果、旧船着場は現在の公園より下流、今の駐車場近くにあったと分かりました。

slashRows.en: The project labeled the two sites separately and explained why the shared name could be misleading.
slashRows.jp: 調査では二地点を別々に示し、共通名が誤解を招く理由も説明しました。

slashRows.en: Students also avoided saying the parking area itself had existed when the landing was active.
slashRows.jp: また船着場時代から駐車場があったとは表現しませんでした。

slashRows.en: Their final map used dates and a surviving landmark to connect old and modern geography accurately.
slashRows.jp: 最終地図は年代と残る目印を使い、昔と今の地理を正確につなぎました。

slashRows.en: They learned that a place name can move or be reused, so matching names alone does not prove matching locations.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは、地名は移動したり再利用されたりするため、名前の一致だけでは場所の一致を証明しないと学びました。

title: The Butterfly Survey That Began at the Same Flower Bed Every Day
sentences: A biology club surveyed butterflies in the school garden for ten mornings.
Every day, members began at the bright flower bed beside the south gate and walked the same route.
Their results showed many butterflies near the south gate and very few near the shaded north trees.
The club first planned to report that butterflies strongly preferred the south side of the garden.
Then a student noticed that the survey always reached the north side nearly twenty minutes later.
Butterfly activity could change as the morning warmed, so location and observation time had been linked together.
For another week, the club alternated starting at the north and south ends.
They still saw more butterflies near the sunny flowers, but the difference was smaller than in the first survey.
The report included both weeks and explained the route-order problem in the first method.
The club suggested repeating the study in another season before making a general claim about the whole year.
They learned that a sampling route can bias a result when place and time always change together.
Changing the starting point made their comparison more balanced without erasing the pattern they had actually observed.

slashRows.en: A biology club surveyed butterflies in the school garden for ten mornings.
slashRows.jp: 生物部は十日間の朝、学校菜園でチョウを調査しました。

slashRows.en: Every day, members began at the bright flower bed beside the south gate and walked the same route.
slashRows.jp: 毎日、南門横の明るい花壇から始め、同じ道順を歩きました。

slashRows.en: Their results showed many butterflies near the south gate and very few near the shaded north trees.
slashRows.jp: 結果は南門近くに多く、北の木陰では非常に少ないと示しました。

slashRows.en: The club first planned to report that butterflies strongly preferred the south side of the garden.
slashRows.jp: 部は最初、チョウが庭の南側を強く好むと報告しようとしました。

slashRows.en: Then a student noticed that the survey always reached the north side nearly twenty minutes later.
slashRows.jp: しかし、調査はいつも北側へ約二十分後に着くと気づきました。

slashRows.en: Butterfly activity could change as the morning warmed, so location and observation time had been linked together.
slashRows.jp: 朝の気温上昇で活動が変わる可能性があり、場所と観察時刻が結びついていました。

slashRows.en: For another week, the club alternated starting at the north and south ends.
slashRows.jp: 次の一週間は北端と南端から交互に始めました。

slashRows.en: They still saw more butterflies near the sunny flowers, but the difference was smaller than in the first survey.
slashRows.jp: 日なたの花近くに多い傾向は残りましたが、最初より差は小さくなりました。

slashRows.en: The report included both weeks and explained the route-order problem in the first method.
slashRows.jp: 報告は両方の週を載せ、最初の方法の道順問題も説明しました。

slashRows.en: The club suggested repeating the study in another season before making a general claim about the whole year.
slashRows.jp: 一年全体の一般的結論を出す前に別季節でも繰り返すよう提案しました。

slashRows.en: They learned that a sampling route can bias a result when place and time always change together.
slashRows.jp: 部は、場所と時刻が常に一緒に変わると調査経路が結果を偏らせることがあると学びました。

slashRows.en: Changing the starting point made their comparison more balanced without erasing the pattern they had actually observed.
slashRows.jp: 開始地点を変えることで、実際に見た傾向を消さず比較をより公平にできました。

title: The Vacant Lot Proposed as a Rain Garden
sentences: A vacant lot near a row of houses filled with shallow water after strong rain.
A neighborhood group proposed turning part of it into a rain garden that could temporarily hold storm water.
The first drawing used almost the whole lot for low ground, stones, and water-loving plants.
Several residents liked the flood idea but said children currently used the dry side of the lot for small games.
An older resident also asked who would remove litter and care for plants after the first year.
The group realized that solving drainage by removing every other use could create a different community problem.
They measured where water actually collected after two more storms.
Most water entered from the road side and stayed in the eastern half of the lot.
The western half drained quickly and was the area children used most often.
A landscape volunteer suggested placing the rain garden only in the eastern half and adding a raised path around it.
The revised design kept an open dry area on the west and connected it to the sidewalk.
Native plants were chosen because they could handle both wet periods and several dry days.
The group found monthly maintenance was not enough during the first summer.
A nearby apartment association agreed to rotate weekly checks for litter and blocked drains during that season.
The city approved a one-year trial and asked the group to photograph water levels after major storms.
During the first rainy season, water stayed in the garden instead of spreading across the whole lot twice.
Children continued using the western side after the ground dried, and the raised path kept people out of the wet planting area.
The group still recorded one blocked drain and changed its maintenance checklist rather than calling the trial perfect.
The proposal succeeded because it reduced one flood problem while preserving another valued use and assigning ongoing work.
Residents learned that practical design must fit water, maintenance, and current users.

slashRows.en: A vacant lot near a row of houses filled with shallow water after strong rain.
slashRows.jp: 住宅地近くの空き地は強い雨の後、浅い水でいっぱいになりました。

slashRows.en: A neighborhood group proposed turning part of it into a rain garden that could temporarily hold storm water.
slashRows.jp: 地域グループは、その一部を雨水を一時的にためるレインガーデンにする案を出しました。

slashRows.en: The first drawing used almost the whole lot for low ground, stones, and water-loving plants.
slashRows.jp: 最初の図面では空き地のほぼ全部を低い地面、石、水を好む植物に使いました。

slashRows.en: Several residents liked the flood idea but said children currently used the dry side of the lot for small games.
slashRows.jp: 洪水対策には賛成する住民も、子どもが今は乾いた側で遊んでいると話しました。

slashRows.en: An older resident also asked who would remove litter and care for plants after the first year.
slashRows.jp: 高齢の住民は、一年目の後に誰がごみを取り植物を世話するのかも尋ねました。

slashRows.en: The group realized that solving drainage by removing every other use could create a different community problem.
slashRows.jp: 排水を解決するため他の利用をすべてなくすと、別の地域問題を作ると気づきました。

slashRows.en: They measured where water actually collected after two more storms.
slashRows.jp: さらに二回の嵐の後、水が実際にたまる場所を測りました。

slashRows.en: Most water entered from the road side and stayed in the eastern half of the lot.
slashRows.jp: 水の大部分は道路側から入り、空き地の東半分に残りました。

slashRows.en: The western half drained quickly and was the area children used most often.
slashRows.jp: 西半分は早く乾き、子どもが最もよく使う場所でした。

slashRows.en: A landscape volunteer suggested placing the rain garden only in the eastern half and adding a raised path around it.
slashRows.jp: 造園ボランティアは、東半分だけをレインガーデンにし、その周りに高い通路を作る案を出しました。

slashRows.en: The revised design kept an open dry area on the west and connected it to the sidewalk.
slashRows.jp: 修正版では西側に乾いた広場を残し、歩道とつなげました。

slashRows.en: Native plants were chosen because they could handle both wet periods and several dry days.
slashRows.jp: 在来植物は湿った時期と数日の乾燥の両方に耐えられるため選ばれました。

slashRows.en: The group found monthly maintenance was not enough during the first summer.
slashRows.jp: グループは、最初の夏は月一回の管理では足りないと分かりました。

slashRows.en: A nearby apartment association agreed to rotate weekly checks for litter and blocked drains during that season.
slashRows.jp: 近くの集合住宅の会が、その季節はごみと排水口を週ごとに交代で確認することに同意しました。

slashRows.en: The city approved a one-year trial and asked the group to photograph water levels after major storms.
slashRows.jp: 市は一年間の試行を認め、大雨後の水位を写真で記録するよう求めました。

slashRows.en: During the first rainy season, water stayed in the garden instead of spreading across the whole lot twice.
slashRows.jp: 最初の雨季には二度、水が空き地全体へ広がらず庭の中にとどまりました。

slashRows.en: Children continued using the western side after the ground dried, and the raised path kept people out of the wet planting area.
slashRows.jp: 地面が乾いた後も子どもは西側を使い、高い通路によって人が湿った植栽部へ入らずに済みました。

slashRows.en: The group still recorded one blocked drain and changed its maintenance checklist rather than calling the trial perfect.
slashRows.jp: 排水口の詰まりが一度あり、試行を完璧とせず管理チェック表を修正しました。

slashRows.en: The proposal succeeded because it reduced one flood problem while preserving another valued use and assigning ongoing work.
slashRows.jp: この案は洪水問題を減らしながら別の大切な利用を残し、継続作業も決めたため成立しました。

slashRows.en: Residents learned that practical design must fit water, maintenance, and current users.
slashRows.jp: 住民は、実用的な設計には水、管理、現在の利用者を合わせる必要があると学びました。

title: The Later School Start Trial and the Morning Bus Problem
sentences: A junior high school considered starting first period thirty minutes later for one month.
Students felt tired in early classes, so the health committee tested extra morning time.
The first proposal simply moved every morning activity and the first bell thirty minutes later.
A transport manager pointed out that the school shared buses with an elementary school whose schedule would not change.
If the same buses arrived thirty minutes later, they would still be carrying elementary students on part of the route.
The committee realized that a classroom schedule could not be changed without checking how students reached school.
It surveyed families and found that sixty-two percent used school buses at least three mornings each week.
Some families could drive later, but many said work schedules made that difficult.
The transport company could provide one extra bus, but not enough vehicles to copy the entire route system at a new time.
Instead of canceling the idea, the school designed a smaller trial for students on two routes that the extra bus could cover.
Participation was voluntary, and students on other routes kept the normal start so transport remained available.
Teachers compared attendance, first-period alertness surveys, and late arrivals for the trial group before and during the month.
Most participants reported feeling less sleepy, and late arrivals did not increase.
However, several families disliked having siblings at different schools leave home at more widely separated times.
Teachers warned that the volunteer group might differ from all students.
The report therefore did not claim that a later start was proven best for everyone.
It concluded that sleep-related benefits looked promising but transport capacity and family schedules were major limits.
For the next year, the school asked the bus company to study a route redesign before any larger experiment.
Families could comment on several start-time options instead of only one.
The school learned that start-time changes must fit transport, families, and trial limits.

slashRows.en: A junior high school considered starting first period thirty minutes later for one month.
slashRows.jp: 中学校は一か月、一時間目を三十分遅く始めることを検討しました。

slashRows.en: Students felt tired in early classes, so the health committee tested extra morning time.
slashRows.jp: 生徒は朝の授業で疲れを感じており、保健委員会は朝の時間を増やす試行をしました。

slashRows.en: The first proposal simply moved every morning activity and the first bell thirty minutes later.
slashRows.jp: 最初の案は朝のすべての活動と始業ベルを三十分後へ動かすだけでした。

slashRows.en: A transport manager pointed out that the school shared buses with an elementary school whose schedule would not change.
slashRows.jp: 交通担当者は、学校が開始時刻を変えない小学校とバスを共有していると指摘しました。

slashRows.en: If the same buses arrived thirty minutes later, they would still be carrying elementary students on part of the route.
slashRows.jp: 同じバスを三十分遅くすると、その時間帯の一部ではまだ小学生を運んでいます。

slashRows.en: The committee realized that a classroom schedule could not be changed without checking how students reached school.
slashRows.jp: 委員会は、登校方法を確認せず授業時刻だけを変えられないと気づきました。

slashRows.en: It surveyed families and found that sixty-two percent used school buses at least three mornings each week.
slashRows.jp: 家庭調査では六十二パーセントが週三朝以上スクールバスを使っていました。

slashRows.en: Some families could drive later, but many said work schedules made that difficult.
slashRows.jp: 遅く送れる家庭もありましたが、仕事のため難しい家庭も多くありました。

slashRows.en: The transport company could provide one extra bus, but not enough vehicles to copy the entire route system at a new time.
slashRows.jp: 交通会社は一台追加できましたが、全路線を別時刻で再現するほど車両はありませんでした。

slashRows.en: Instead of canceling the idea, the school designed a smaller trial for students on two routes that the extra bus could cover.
slashRows.jp: 案をやめず、追加バスで対応できる二路線の生徒だけを対象に小規模試行を設計しました。

slashRows.en: Participation was voluntary, and students on other routes kept the normal start so transport remained available.
slashRows.jp: 参加は任意で、ほかの路線の生徒は交通を確保するため通常開始を続けました。

slashRows.en: Teachers compared attendance, first-period alertness surveys, and late arrivals for the trial group before and during the month.
slashRows.jp: 先生は試行班の出席、一時間目の覚醒度調査、遅刻を試行前と期間中で比べました。

slashRows.en: Most participants reported feeling less sleepy, and late arrivals did not increase.
slashRows.jp: 多くの参加者は眠気が減ったと答え、遅刻も増えませんでした。

slashRows.en: However, several families disliked having siblings at different schools leave home at more widely separated times.
slashRows.jp: 一方、兄弟が別の学校へより離れた時刻に出ることを不便に感じる家庭もありました。

slashRows.en: Teachers warned that the volunteer group might differ from all students.
slashRows.jp: 先生は、希望者集団が全生徒と異なる可能性を指摘しました。

slashRows.en: The report therefore did not claim that a later start was proven best for everyone.
slashRows.jp: そこで報告は、遅い開始が全員に最良と証明されたとはしませんでした。

slashRows.en: It concluded that sleep-related benefits looked promising but transport capacity and family schedules were major limits.
slashRows.jp: 睡眠面の利点は有望だが、交通容量と家庭予定が大きな制約だと結論づけました。

slashRows.en: For the next year, the school asked the bus company to study a route redesign before any larger experiment.
slashRows.jp: 翌年に向け、より大きな実験前にバス会社へ路線再設計の検討を依頼しました。

slashRows.en: Families could comment on several start-time options instead of only one.
slashRows.jp: 家庭は一案だけでなく複数の開始時刻案へ意見を出せました。

slashRows.en: The school learned that start-time changes must fit transport, families, and trial limits.
slashRows.jp: 学校は、開始時刻変更には交通、家庭、試行の限界を合わせる必要があると学びました。

title: The Reusable Cup Deposit Trial at a Community Event
sentences: A community festival usually used thousands of disposable drink cups during one weekend.
Organizers proposed a reusable cup system with a two-hundred-yen deposit returned when visitors brought cups back.
They expected most visitors to return cups because they would want the money back.
Several food vendors worried that collecting, stacking, and counting used cups would slow already busy serving lines.
The first design placed return boxes at every drink stall.
During a small rehearsal, customers returning cups crossed the same space as people buying drinks, creating confusion.
Organizers realized that a good environmental idea could fail if the return process created too much work at the wrong place.
They moved returns to three separate stations near the main exits and assigned volunteers only to cup collection.
Vendors then needed only to hand out clean cups and collect the deposit with each drink sale.
At the first full festival day, 1,240 cups were issued and 1,083 were returned by closing time.
Missing cups still mattered because replacements used money and resources.
A short visitor survey found that some people had left through a small side gate where no return station was visible.
Others said they had not understood that cups could be returned at any of the three stations rather than only near the original vendor.
For the second day, organizers added return signs at every exit and printed the three-station rule on drink tickets.
The side gate also received a small collection point during the final hour, when many families left at once.
The return rate improved, while vendors reported no longer lines than under the old disposable system.
Volunteers did spend significant time washing and checking cups after the event, so the report included labor as well as waste reduction.
The next festival kept the deposit but budgeted a washing team and improved exit signs from the beginning.
Organizers learned that reuse needs convenient returns, clear information, and realistic staff work.

slashRows.en: A community festival usually used thousands of disposable drink cups during one weekend.
slashRows.jp: 地域祭りでは通常、一週末に何千個もの使い捨てカップを使っていました。

slashRows.en: Organizers proposed a reusable cup system with a two-hundred-yen deposit returned when visitors brought cups back.
slashRows.jp: 主催者は、返却時に二百円が戻るデポジット式の再利用カップを提案しました。

slashRows.en: They expected most visitors to return cups because they would want the money back.
slashRows.jp: 来場者は返金を受けたいので大部分が返すだろうと予想しました。

slashRows.en: Several food vendors worried that collecting, stacking, and counting used cups would slow already busy serving lines.
slashRows.jp: 食品店は、使用済みカップの回収、積み重ね、数え作業で混雑した販売列がさらに遅くなると心配しました。

slashRows.en: The first design placed return boxes at every drink stall.
slashRows.jp: 最初の設計では各飲料店に返却箱を置きました。

slashRows.en: During a small rehearsal, customers returning cups crossed the same space as people buying drinks, creating confusion.
slashRows.jp: 小さな試行では返却客と購入客が同じ場所を通り、混乱が起きました。

slashRows.en: Organizers realized that a good environmental idea could fail if the return process created too much work at the wrong place.
slashRows.jp: 主催者は、環境によい案も返却作業が不適切な場所で負担を増やせば失敗すると気づきました。

slashRows.en: They moved returns to three separate stations near the main exits and assigned volunteers only to cup collection.
slashRows.jp: 返却を主な出口近くの三つの専用場所へ移し、カップ回収だけを担当するボランティアを置きました。

slashRows.en: Vendors then needed only to hand out clean cups and collect the deposit with each drink sale.
slashRows.jp: 店舗は清潔なカップを渡し、飲料販売時にデポジットを受け取るだけで済みました。

slashRows.en: At the first full festival day, 1,240 cups were issued and 1,083 were returned by closing time.
slashRows.jp: 本番初日は一二四〇個を貸し出し、閉場までに一〇八三個が返却されました。

slashRows.en: Missing cups still mattered because replacements used money and resources.
slashRows.jp: 未返却カップは交換に費用と資源が必要なため問題でした。

slashRows.en: A short visitor survey found that some people had left through a small side gate where no return station was visible.
slashRows.jp: 来場者調査では、返却場所が見えない小さな脇門から帰った人がいると分かりました。

slashRows.en: Others said they had not understood that cups could be returned at any of the three stations rather than only near the original vendor.
slashRows.jp: 元の店の近くだけでなく三か所どこでも返せると理解していない人もいました。

slashRows.en: For the second day, organizers added return signs at every exit and printed the three-station rule on drink tickets.
slashRows.jp: 二日目は全出口に返却表示を付け、飲料券にも三か所返却の規則を印刷しました。

slashRows.en: The side gate also received a small collection point during the final hour, when many families left at once.
slashRows.jp: 多くの家族が一斉に帰る最後の一時間は脇門にも小さな回収所を置きました。

slashRows.en: The return rate improved, while vendors reported no longer lines than under the old disposable system.
slashRows.jp: 返却率は上がり、店舗は旧使い捨て方式より列が長くならなかったと報告しました。

slashRows.en: Volunteers did spend significant time washing and checking cups after the event, so the report included labor as well as waste reduction.
slashRows.jp: 一方、ボランティアは行事後の洗浄と確認にかなり時間を使ったため、報告はごみ削減だけでなく労力も含めました。

slashRows.en: The next festival kept the deposit but budgeted a washing team and improved exit signs from the beginning.
slashRows.jp: 次回はデポジットを続け、最初から洗浄班の予算と出口表示を用意しました。

slashRows.en: Organizers learned that reuse needs convenient returns, clear information, and realistic staff work.
slashRows.jp: 主催者は、再利用には便利な返却、明確な情報、現実的な人員作業が必要だと学びました。

title: The Community Repair Cafe and Who Could Take Part
sentences: A youth group proposed a monthly repair cafe where residents could bring broken household objects and learn simple fixes.
The first plan invited anyone to work directly with volunteer tools after signing a short form.
Experienced volunteers liked the open atmosphere, but the community center manager asked about children, electrical devices, and sharp tools.
The group realized that equal access did not mean every visitor should perform every repair without limits.
They listed common tasks and divided them by risk rather than by the age of the object owner.
Sewing a loose button and tightening a simple screw were placed in a guided low-risk area.
Repairs involving mains electricity, damaged batteries, gas, or high heat were excluded from public work tables.
Children could take part in low-risk work with a guardian and a volunteer present.
The group also noticed an access problem: all work tables in the first room were high and had fixed stools.
One volunteer who used a wheelchair suggested adding two lower tables with clear space underneath.
The organizers borrowed adjustable lamps and placed commonly used hand tools where they could be reached from seated positions.
For the first event, every object received a short safety check before a visitor entered a work area.
Volunteers wrote 'repair not attempted' on items that fell outside the safe rules instead of experimenting with them.
Forty-seven objects were brought in, and thirty-one received some safe repair or adjustment.
Seven owners learned to make a small repair themselves under guidance rather than simply handing the object to an expert.
Feedback supported learning, but visitors wanted clearer information before bringing heavy items.
The group added an online list of accepted and excluded repair types with photographs of examples.
It also allowed visitors to send a description in advance when they were unsure.
The next event kept broad participation while showing limits before arrival.
The group learned to design access, safety, space, and information together.

slashRows.en: A youth group proposed a monthly repair cafe where residents could bring broken household objects and learn simple fixes.
slashRows.jp: 青少年グループは、住民が壊れた家庭用品を持ち寄り簡単な修理を学ぶ月一回のリペアカフェを提案しました。

slashRows.en: The first plan invited anyone to work directly with volunteer tools after signing a short form.
slashRows.jp: 最初の案では短い用紙に署名すれば誰でもボランティアの工具を直接使えるようにしました。

slashRows.en: Experienced volunteers liked the open atmosphere, but the community center manager asked about children, electrical devices, and sharp tools.
slashRows.jp: 経験あるボランティアは開放的な雰囲気を好みましたが、地域センター管理者は子ども、電気製品、鋭い工具について尋ねました。

slashRows.en: The group realized that equal access did not mean every visitor should perform every repair without limits.
slashRows.jp: グループは、平等な参加とは全員が制限なくすべての修理をすることではないと気づきました。

slashRows.en: They listed common tasks and divided them by risk rather than by the age of the object owner.
slashRows.jp: よくある作業を一覧にし、持ち主の年齢ではなく危険度で分けました。

slashRows.en: Sewing a loose button and tightening a simple screw were placed in a guided low-risk area.
slashRows.jp: 取れかけたボタン縫いと簡単なねじ締めは案内付き低危険区域にしました。

slashRows.en: Repairs involving mains electricity, damaged batteries, gas, or high heat were excluded from public work tables.
slashRows.jp: 家庭用電源、傷んだ電池、ガス、高熱に関わる修理は一般作業台から除外しました。

slashRows.en: Children could take part in low-risk work with a guardian and a volunteer present.
slashRows.jp: 子どもは保護者とボランティアがいれば低危険作業へ参加できました。

slashRows.en: The group also noticed an access problem: all work tables in the first room were high and had fixed stools.
slashRows.jp: さらに最初の部屋の作業台はすべて高く固定椅子で、利用しにくさもありました。

slashRows.en: One volunteer who used a wheelchair suggested adding two lower tables with clear space underneath.
slashRows.jp: 車いす利用のボランティアが、下に空間のある低い机を二台加えるよう提案しました。

slashRows.en: The organizers borrowed adjustable lamps and placed commonly used hand tools where they could be reached from seated positions.
slashRows.jp: 主催者は調整式ライトを借り、よく使う手工具を座った位置から届く場所へ置きました。

slashRows.en: For the first event, every object received a short safety check before a visitor entered a work area.
slashRows.jp: 初回行事では、来場者が作業区域へ入る前にすべての物を短く安全確認しました。

slashRows.en: Volunteers wrote 'repair not attempted' on items that fell outside the safe rules instead of experimenting with them.
slashRows.jp: 安全規則外の物には試しに触らず「修理未実施」と記録しました。

slashRows.en: Forty-seven objects were brought in, and thirty-one received some safe repair or adjustment.
slashRows.jp: 四十七個が持ち込まれ、三十一個に安全な修理や調整が行われました。

slashRows.en: Seven owners learned to make a small repair themselves under guidance rather than simply handing the object to an expert.
slashRows.jp: 七人の持ち主は専門家へ渡すだけでなく、案内を受けて小さな修理を自分で行いました。

slashRows.en: Feedback supported learning, but visitors wanted clearer information before bringing heavy items.
slashRows.jp: 感想では学習への支持があり、重い物を運ぶ前の明確な情報も求められました。

slashRows.en: The group added an online list of accepted and excluded repair types with photographs of examples.
slashRows.jp: グループは受け付ける修理と除外する修理を例写真付きでオンライン掲載しました。

slashRows.en: It also allowed visitors to send a description in advance when they were unsure.
slashRows.jp: 判断に迷う場合は事前に説明を送れるようにもしました。

slashRows.en: The next event kept broad participation while showing limits before arrival.
slashRows.jp: 次回も広い参加を保ち、来場前に制限を示しました。

slashRows.en: The group learned to design access, safety, space, and information together.
slashRows.jp: グループは、参加、安全、空間、情報を一緒に設計すると学びました。

title: The Science Museum, Train Timetable, Planetarium Seats, Lunch Windows, and Floor Map
sentences: Four students planned a Saturday trip to a science museum by train.
They wanted to see a robotics show, attend one planetarium program, eat lunch, and return home before five.
The train table showed arrivals at Museum Station at nine forty, ten twenty, and eleven ten.
The robotics show began at ten thirty on the second floor and lasted forty minutes.
Planetarium programs began at eleven thirty and one thirty, with only six seats left for the morning show and forty seats left for the afternoon show.
The floor map showed eight minutes from the entrance to robotics, five minutes from robotics to the planetarium, and seven minutes from the planetarium to the lunch area.
At first, the group chose the ten twenty train because it seemed to arrive before the ten thirty robotics show.
They then noticed that station arrival was not museum entrance time and the walk from the station to the entrance took six minutes.
Even without any delay, arriving at ten twenty would leave only four minutes after reaching the entrance, less than the eight-minute indoor walk.
The nine forty train would reach the entrance around nine forty-six and leave enough time for the show.
After robotics ended at eleven ten, the students could reach the planetarium by eleven fifteen.
Because only six morning seats remained, they reserved four before the trip instead of assuming seats would stay open.
The morning program ended at twelve ten, and the lunch area was a seven-minute walk away.
The cafeteria had two lunch windows, eleven thirty to twelve forty-five and one fifteen to two thirty.
They could reach lunch around twelve seventeen, inside the first window, without giving up the morning planetarium seats.
The students allowed forty minutes for eating and then visited the energy gallery on the first floor.
Their preferred return train left Museum Station at four twenty and arrived home station at four fifty-five.
The map gave six minutes from the museum entrance back to the station, so the group set a four o'clock meeting time at the entrance.
That left extra time for buying tickets and for a slow crossing near the station.
On the day, the robotics show started five minutes late, but the reserved planetarium seats were held until eleven twenty-five.
The group still reached the planetarium before that limit and completed the rest of the plan.
They boarded the four twenty train and reached home station before five as required.
The students learned that a workable museum schedule must combine train arrival, outside and inside walking time, seat availability, program length, and meal windows.

slashRows.en: Four students planned a Saturday trip to a science museum by train.
slashRows.jp: 四人の生徒が土曜日に電車で科学博物館へ行く計画を立てました。

slashRows.en: They wanted to see a robotics show, attend one planetarium program, eat lunch, and return home before five.
slashRows.jp: ロボット実演、プラネタリウム一回、昼食を楽しみ、五時前に帰宅したいと考えました。

slashRows.en: The train table showed arrivals at Museum Station at nine forty, ten twenty, and eleven ten.
slashRows.jp: 時刻表では博物館駅への到着が九時四十分、十時二十分、十一時十分でした。

slashRows.en: The robotics show began at ten thirty on the second floor and lasted forty minutes.
slashRows.jp: ロボット実演は二階で十時半開始、四十分間でした。

slashRows.en: Planetarium programs began at eleven thirty and one thirty, with only six seats left for the morning show and forty seats left for the afternoon show.
slashRows.jp: プラネタリウムは十一時半と一時半で、午前は残席六、午後は四十席でした。

slashRows.en: The floor map showed eight minutes from the entrance to robotics, five minutes from robotics to the planetarium, and seven minutes from the planetarium to the lunch area.
slashRows.jp: 館内図では入口からロボットまで八分、ロボットからプラネタリウム五分、そこから昼食場所七分でした。

slashRows.en: At first, the group chose the ten twenty train because it seemed to arrive before the ten thirty robotics show.
slashRows.jp: 最初、十時半の実演より前に着くので十時二十分着の電車を選びました。

slashRows.en: They then noticed that station arrival was not museum entrance time and the walk from the station to the entrance took six minutes.
slashRows.jp: しかし駅到着は博物館入口到着ではなく、駅から入口まで徒歩六分かかると気づきました。

slashRows.en: Even without any delay, arriving at ten twenty would leave only four minutes after reaching the entrance, less than the eight-minute indoor walk.
slashRows.jp: 遅れがなくても十時二十分着では入口到着後四分しかなく、館内移動八分に足りません。

slashRows.en: The nine forty train would reach the entrance around nine forty-six and leave enough time for the show.
slashRows.jp: 九時四十分着なら九時四十六分ごろ入口に着き、実演まで十分時間があります。

slashRows.en: After robotics ended at eleven ten, the students could reach the planetarium by eleven fifteen.
slashRows.jp: 実演が十一時十分に終わると、十一時十五分にはプラネタリウムへ着けます。

slashRows.en: Because only six morning seats remained, they reserved four before the trip instead of assuming seats would stay open.
slashRows.jp: 午前は残席六だけなので、席が残ると決めつけず旅行前に四席予約しました。

slashRows.en: The morning program ended at twelve ten, and the lunch area was a seven-minute walk away.
slashRows.jp: 午前のプログラムは十二時十分終了で、昼食場所は徒歩七分でした。

slashRows.en: The cafeteria had two lunch windows, eleven thirty to twelve forty-five and one fifteen to two thirty.
slashRows.jp: 食堂の昼食時間は十一時半から十二時四十五分と、一時十五分から二時半の二つでした。

slashRows.en: They could reach lunch around twelve seventeen, inside the first window, without giving up the morning planetarium seats.
slashRows.jp: 十二時十七分ごろ昼食へ着けるため、午前のプラネタリウムを諦めず最初の昼食時間に間に合います。

slashRows.en: The students allowed forty minutes for eating and then visited the energy gallery on the first floor.
slashRows.jp: 生徒は昼食に四十分取り、その後一階のエネルギー展示を見ました。

slashRows.en: Their preferred return train left Museum Station at four twenty and arrived home station at four fifty-five.
slashRows.jp: 希望する帰りの電車は博物館駅を四時二十分に出て、地元駅へ四時五十五分に着きます。

slashRows.en: The map gave six minutes from the museum entrance back to the station, so the group set a four o'clock meeting time at the entrance.
slashRows.jp: 入口から駅までは六分なので、四時に入口集合と決めました。

slashRows.en: That left extra time for buying tickets and for a slow crossing near the station.
slashRows.jp: これで切符購入や駅近くのゆっくりした横断にも余裕があります。

slashRows.en: On the day, the robotics show started five minutes late, but the reserved planetarium seats were held until eleven twenty-five.
slashRows.jp: 当日、ロボット実演は五分遅れましたが、予約席は十一時二十五分まで確保されていました。

slashRows.en: The group still reached the planetarium before that limit and completed the rest of the plan.
slashRows.jp: グループは締切前に到着し、その後の予定も実行できました。

slashRows.en: They boarded the four twenty train and reached home station before five as required.
slashRows.jp: 四時二十分の電車に乗り、条件どおり五時前に地元駅へ着きました。

slashRows.en: The students learned that a workable museum schedule must combine train arrival, outside and inside walking time, seat availability, program length, and meal windows.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは、実行できる博物館予定には電車到着、館外と館内の徒歩時間、席数、行事時間、食事時間帯を組み合わせる必要があると学びました。

title: The Farm Market Orders, Harvest Table, Cooler Capacity, Delivery Routes, and Time Rules
sentences: A school agriculture club planned to deliver vegetable boxes to three community markets on Saturday.
The club had to fill confirmed orders without carrying more chilled produce than its cooler could safely hold.
The harvest table listed forty boxes of tomatoes, twenty-eight boxes of lettuce, and thirty-two boxes of carrots ready by seven thirty.
Market A ordered twelve tomato, eight lettuce, and ten carrot boxes; Market B ordered fifteen, ten, and eight; Market C ordered ten, eight, and twelve.
The orders totaled thirty-seven tomato, twenty-six lettuce, and thirty carrot boxes, so the harvest could cover every confirmed order.
However, lettuce had to stay chilled, and the van cooler held only eighteen lettuce boxes at one time.
The route table showed twenty minutes from school to Market A, fifteen more to B, and twenty-five from B to C.
A time rule said all lettuce must reach a market within sixty minutes after leaving the school cooler.
At first, students planned to load all twenty-six lettuce boxes and visit A, B, then C in one trip.
That plan failed immediately because twenty-six exceeded the van cooler's capacity of eighteen.
They considered loading A and B lettuce together, which required exactly eighteen boxes.
The van could reach A in twenty minutes and B thirty-five minutes after leaving school, both inside the sixty-minute rule.
After delivering to B, the van would return to school to collect Market C's eight chilled boxes.
A different direct road from B back to school took twenty-five minutes, and school to C directly took thirty minutes.
That meant C's lettuce could leave school on the second trip and arrive thirty minutes later, safely inside the rule.
Tomatoes and carrots for C could wait in the covered loading area.
Students checked market opening times next: A opened at eight thirty, B at nine, and C at ten.
Leaving school at eight ten would reach A at eight thirty and B at eight forty-five, fifteen minutes before B opened.
The club changed departure to eight twenty-five, reaching A at eight forty-five and B at nine, while keeping both lettuce deliveries within thirty-five minutes.
After unloading at B, the van returned to school, loaded C's order, and left again after a short count check.
It reached C after ten, so the market was already open and no chilled box had spent more than thirty minutes outside the school cooler.
Every order matched the written sheet, and the two-trip plan stayed within harvest, cooler, route, and time limits.
The club learned to check quantity, storage, travel time, and opening rules together.

slashRows.en: A school agriculture club planned to deliver vegetable boxes to three community markets on Saturday.
slashRows.jp: 学校の農業部は土曜日に三つの地域市場へ野菜箱を届ける計画を立てました。

slashRows.en: The club had to fill confirmed orders without carrying more chilled produce than its cooler could safely hold.
slashRows.jp: 確定注文を満たしつつ、保冷庫の安全容量を超えて冷蔵野菜を運ばない必要がありました。

slashRows.en: The harvest table listed forty boxes of tomatoes, twenty-eight boxes of lettuce, and thirty-two boxes of carrots ready by seven thirty.
slashRows.jp: 収穫表では七時半までにトマト四十箱、レタス二十八箱、ニンジン三十二箱が準備できます。

slashRows.en: Market A ordered twelve tomato, eight lettuce, and ten carrot boxes; Market B ordered fifteen, ten, and eight; Market C ordered ten, eight, and twelve.
slashRows.jp: 市場Aはトマト十二、レタス八、ニンジン十箱、市場Bは十五、十、八箱、市場Cは十、八、十二箱を注文しました。

slashRows.en: The orders totaled thirty-seven tomato, twenty-six lettuce, and thirty carrot boxes, so the harvest could cover every confirmed order.
slashRows.jp: 注文合計はトマト三十七、レタス二十六、ニンジン三十箱で、収穫量はすべてを満たせます。

slashRows.en: However, lettuce had to stay chilled, and the van cooler held only eighteen lettuce boxes at one time.
slashRows.jp: しかしレタスは冷蔵が必要で、車の保冷庫は一度に十八箱まででした。

slashRows.en: The route table showed twenty minutes from school to Market A, fifteen more to B, and twenty-five from B to C.
slashRows.jp: 経路表では学校からAまで二十分、AからBへ十五分、BからCへ二十五分でした。

slashRows.en: A time rule said all lettuce must reach a market within sixty minutes after leaving the school cooler.
slashRows.jp: 時間規則ではレタスは学校の保冷庫を出て六十分以内に市場へ着く必要がありました。

slashRows.en: At first, students planned to load all twenty-six lettuce boxes and visit A, B, then C in one trip.
slashRows.jp: 最初、生徒たちはレタス二十六箱を全部積み、A、B、Cを一度で回る予定でした。

slashRows.en: That plan failed immediately because twenty-six exceeded the van cooler's capacity of eighteen.
slashRows.jp: しかし二十六箱は保冷庫容量十八箱を超えるため、その案は成立しませんでした。

slashRows.en: They considered loading A and B lettuce together, which required exactly eighteen boxes.
slashRows.jp: AとBのレタスを合わせるとちょうど十八箱なので、それを一緒に積む案を考えました。

slashRows.en: The van could reach A in twenty minutes and B thirty-five minutes after leaving school, both inside the sixty-minute rule.
slashRows.jp: 学校出発からAは二十分、Bは三十五分で、どちらも六十分以内です。

slashRows.en: After delivering to B, the van would return to school to collect Market C's eight chilled boxes.
slashRows.jp: Bへ届けた後、車は学校へ戻りC用の冷蔵八箱を受け取ることにしました。

slashRows.en: A different direct road from B back to school took twenty-five minutes, and school to C directly took thirty minutes.
slashRows.jp: Bから学校へ戻る別の直通路は二十五分、学校からCへ直接は三十分でした。

slashRows.en: That meant C's lettuce could leave school on the second trip and arrive thirty minutes later, safely inside the rule.
slashRows.jp: つまりCのレタスは二回目に学校を出て三十分後に着き、規則内に収まります。

slashRows.en: Tomatoes and carrots for C could wait in the covered loading area.
slashRows.jp: C用のトマトとニンジンは屋根付き積込所で待機できました。

slashRows.en: Students checked market opening times next: A opened at eight thirty, B at nine, and C at ten.
slashRows.jp: 次に開場時刻を確認すると、Aは八時半、Bは九時、Cは十時でした。

slashRows.en: Leaving school at eight ten would reach A at eight thirty and B at eight forty-five, fifteen minutes before B opened.
slashRows.jp: 八時十分に出るとAへ八時半、Bへ八時四十五分で、Bの開場十五分前です。

slashRows.en: The club changed departure to eight twenty-five, reaching A at eight forty-five and B at nine, while keeping both lettuce deliveries within thirty-five minutes.
slashRows.jp: 出発を八時二十五分に変えるとAへ八時四十五分、Bへ九時で、レタスはどちらも三十五分以内です。

slashRows.en: After unloading at B, the van returned to school, loaded C's order, and left again after a short count check.
slashRows.jp: Bで荷下ろし後、学校へ戻りCの注文を積み、短い数量確認後に再出発しました。

slashRows.en: It reached C after ten, so the market was already open and no chilled box had spent more than thirty minutes outside the school cooler.
slashRows.jp: Cへは十時過ぎに到着し市場は開場済みで、冷蔵箱は学校の保冷庫を出て三十分を超えませんでした。

slashRows.en: Every order matched the written sheet, and the two-trip plan stayed within harvest, cooler, route, and time limits.
slashRows.jp: すべての注文が書面と一致し、二回配送は収穫量、保冷容量、経路、時間条件を満たしました。

slashRows.en: The club learned to check quantity, storage, travel time, and opening rules together.
slashRows.jp: 部は、数量、保管、移動時間、開場規則を一緒に確認すると学びました。

title: The Heavy-Rain Warning, Bridge Closure Map, Shelter Capacity, and Walking Times
sentences: A neighborhood school used a planning exercise to choose a meeting place during very heavy rain.
The class had to move forty students and four teachers from the school to one listed community center.
A map showed two river crossings, East Bridge and Hill Bridge.
The current notice placed the river at Level 3, and the route table marked East Bridge unavailable at that level.
Three meeting places were listed: Community Hall for fifty people, Library Annex for thirty-eight, and Hill Gym for eighty.
Walking times were twelve minutes to Community Hall by East Bridge, twenty-two minutes to the Library Annex, and twenty-eight minutes to Hill Gym by Hill Bridge.
At first, several students selected Community Hall because it was shortest and large enough for forty-four people.
When they linked that choice to the route table, they saw that its required bridge was not available.
The Library Annex did not need a river crossing, but its capacity was six places too small for the whole class group.
The exercise rule said the class should stay together unless staff gave a different instruction.
Hill Gym was therefore the only listed place meeting both route and capacity conditions at Level 3.
Students checked the Hill Bridge note and found that its status would be reviewed if the river moved to Level 4.
Because the walk was twenty-eight minutes, the teacher added another information check immediately before departure.
The newest update still showed Level 3, so Hill Gym remained the planned destination.
The class also marked an indoor waiting point at school in case the route status changed before they left.
Four student leaders carried paper maps so the group would not depend on one phone or one person.
During the practice walk, a fallen branch blocked one side street on the planned route.
The map showed a parallel street that returned to the Hill Bridge route after adding about three minutes.
Teachers used that marked detour and kept the class together rather than sending separate groups in different directions.
The group reached Hill Gym in thirty-one minutes, matching the original twenty-eight-minute estimate plus the detour.
In their review, students explained that Community Hall failed the route condition and Library Annex failed the capacity condition.
They also noted that Hill Gym was a decision for the current Level 3 information, not a permanent answer for every situation.
The class learned that a workable route plan must connect current information, route availability, capacity, walking time, and a clear alternative.

slashRows.en: A neighborhood school used a planning exercise to choose a meeting place during very heavy rain.
slashRows.jp: 地域の学校は非常に強い雨のときの集合場所を選ぶ計画演習を行いました。

slashRows.en: The class had to move forty students and four teachers from the school to one listed community center.
slashRows.jp: クラスは生徒四十人と先生四人を学校から一覧にある一つの地域施設へ移す必要がありました。

slashRows.en: A map showed two river crossings, East Bridge and Hill Bridge.
slashRows.jp: 地図には東橋と丘橋という二つの川の横断地点がありました。

slashRows.en: The current notice placed the river at Level 3, and the route table marked East Bridge unavailable at that level.
slashRows.jp: 現在の案内は川をレベル3とし、経路表ではそのレベルで東橋は利用不可となっていました。

slashRows.en: Three meeting places were listed: Community Hall for fifty people, Library Annex for thirty-eight, and Hill Gym for eighty.
slashRows.jp: 集合場所は定員五十人の地域ホール、三十八人の図書館別館、八十人の丘体育館でした。

slashRows.en: Walking times were twelve minutes to Community Hall by East Bridge, twenty-two minutes to the Library Annex, and twenty-eight minutes to Hill Gym by Hill Bridge.
slashRows.jp: 徒歩時間は東橋経由の地域ホール十二分、図書館別館二十二分、丘橋経由の丘体育館二十八分でした。

slashRows.en: At first, several students selected Community Hall because it was shortest and large enough for forty-four people.
slashRows.jp: 最初、何人かは最短で四十四人を収容できる地域ホールを選びました。

slashRows.en: When they linked that choice to the route table, they saw that its required bridge was not available.
slashRows.jp: しかし経路表と結びつけると、その場所へ必要な橋が利用できないと分かりました。

slashRows.en: The Library Annex did not need a river crossing, but its capacity was six places too small for the whole class group.
slashRows.jp: 図書館別館は川を渡りませんが、クラス全体には六人分定員が足りませんでした。

slashRows.en: The exercise rule said the class should stay together unless staff gave a different instruction.
slashRows.jp: 演習規則では、別の職員指示がない限りクラスは一緒に行動するとされていました。

slashRows.en: Hill Gym was therefore the only listed place meeting both route and capacity conditions at Level 3.
slashRows.jp: そのためレベル3で経路と定員の両方を満たす一覧先は丘体育館だけでした。

slashRows.en: Students checked the Hill Bridge note and found that its status would be reviewed if the river moved to Level 4.
slashRows.jp: 生徒が丘橋の注記を見ると、川がレベル4になれば利用状況を再確認すると分かりました。

slashRows.en: Because the walk was twenty-eight minutes, the teacher added another information check immediately before departure.
slashRows.jp: 徒歩が二十八分あるため、先生は出発直前に情報をもう一度確認することにしました。

slashRows.en: The newest update still showed Level 3, so Hill Gym remained the planned destination.
slashRows.jp: 最新情報もレベル3だったため、丘体育館を計画上の目的地としました。

slashRows.en: The class also marked an indoor waiting point at school in case the route status changed before they left.
slashRows.jp: 出発前に経路状況が変わった場合に備え、学校内の待機場所も決めました。

slashRows.en: Four student leaders carried paper maps so the group would not depend on one phone or one person.
slashRows.jp: 一台の携帯や一人だけに頼らないよう、四人の生徒リーダーが紙の地図を持ちました。

slashRows.en: During the practice walk, a fallen branch blocked one side street on the planned route.
slashRows.jp: 練習歩行中、予定経路の脇道一本が倒れた枝で塞がれていました。

slashRows.en: The map showed a parallel street that returned to the Hill Bridge route after adding about three minutes.
slashRows.jp: 地図には約三分追加で丘橋経路へ戻れる平行道路がありました。

slashRows.en: Teachers used that marked detour and kept the class together rather than sending separate groups in different directions.
slashRows.jp: 先生はその記載された迂回路を使い、班を別方向へ分けずクラスを一緒に保ちました。

slashRows.en: The group reached Hill Gym in thirty-one minutes, matching the original twenty-eight-minute estimate plus the detour.
slashRows.jp: グループは三十一分で丘体育館へ着き、元の二十八分に迂回三分を加えた時間と一致しました。

slashRows.en: In their review, students explained that Community Hall failed the route condition and Library Annex failed the capacity condition.
slashRows.jp: 振り返りでは、地域ホールは経路条件、図書館別館は定員条件を満たさないと説明しました。

slashRows.en: They also noted that Hill Gym was a decision for the current Level 3 information, not a permanent answer for every situation.
slashRows.jp: 丘体育館は現在のレベル3情報に基づく判断であり、すべての状況で固定の答えではないとも記しました。

slashRows.en: The class learned that a workable route plan must connect current information, route availability, capacity, walking time, and a clear alternative.
slashRows.jp: クラスは、実行できる経路計画には最新情報、経路利用状況、定員、徒歩時間、明確な代替案を結びつける必要があると学びました。

title: The Summer Sports Day, Heat Index Table, Shade Map, Water Stations, and Match Times
sentences: A junior high school planned a summer sports day with outdoor matches from nine in the morning until two thirty.
Two days before the event, the forecast showed higher temperatures than the school had expected.
A heat-index table listed 29 at nine, 32 at eleven, 35 at one, and 34 at two.
The school guideline called for extra breaks above 31 and moving hard outdoor activities to another time or place at 35 or higher.
The field map showed a large shaded gym entrance on the west side and a smaller tree area on the east.
Water Station A stood beside the gym, Station B was near the center field, and Station C was beside the east gate.
The original match table placed long-distance running at one and the soccer final at one forty.
At first, organizers planned to keep the schedule and simply add more reminders to drink water.
The planning team noticed that this would not follow the written guideline if the index reached 35 at one.
They moved long-distance running to nine twenty, when the forecast value was still below the extra-break level.
The opening program was shortened slightly, so runners still had time to prepare before the earlier race.
The soccer final was harder to move because both teams also had morning matches.
Organizers prepared an indoor skills final in the gym if the one-o'clock measured index reached 35 or above.
The gym had enough space for both teams and officials but not for every spectator.
A live screen was placed at the large shaded west entrance so additional spectators could watch from outside the playing area.
The shade map also showed that Station B in the center field had no nearby cover at midday.
A temporary canopy and benches were moved to Station B so students could drink while seated out of direct sun.
Each team received a scheduled water break after every match, and teachers kept a simple record of students using the cool rest room.
At twelve thirty, the measured index was 34, so low-intensity outdoor activities continued with the added breaks.
At one, the index reached 35 exactly, so the prepared change for hard outdoor activities was used.
The soccer final changed to the indoor skills format, while a relay planned for later was moved to a cooler practice day.
Families were told the changes followed the measured index and school guideline.
The final report recorded schedule changes, shade, water breaks, and three students who rested for the rest of the event.
The school did not call the day risk-free just because the revised plan worked.
Students learned to combine measured heat, activity level, shade, water, timing, and a change rule.

slashRows.en: A junior high school planned a summer sports day with outdoor matches from nine in the morning until two thirty.
slashRows.jp: 中学校は午前九時から午後二時半まで屋外試合を行う夏の運動会を計画しました。

slashRows.en: Two days before the event, the forecast showed higher temperatures than the school had expected.
slashRows.jp: 行事二日前、予報は学校の予想より高い気温を示しました。

slashRows.en: A heat-index table listed 29 at nine, 32 at eleven, 35 at one, and 34 at two.
slashRows.jp: 暑さ指数表は九時29、十一時32、一時35、二時34でした。

slashRows.en: The school guideline called for extra breaks above 31 and moving hard outdoor activities to another time or place at 35 or higher.
slashRows.jp: 学校の指針では31を超えると休憩を増やし、35以上では激しい屋外活動を別の時刻や場所へ移すことになっていました。

slashRows.en: The field map showed a large shaded gym entrance on the west side and a smaller tree area on the east.
slashRows.jp: 校庭図では西側に大きな体育館入口の日陰、東側に小さな木陰がありました。

slashRows.en: Water Station A stood beside the gym, Station B was near the center field, and Station C was beside the east gate.
slashRows.jp: 給水所Aは体育館横、Bは校庭中央、Cは東門横でした。

slashRows.en: The original match table placed long-distance running at one and the soccer final at one forty.
slashRows.jp: 元の競技表では長距離走が一時、サッカー決勝が一時四十分でした。

slashRows.en: At first, organizers planned to keep the schedule and simply add more reminders to drink water.
slashRows.jp: 最初、主催者は予定を変えず給水の声かけだけ増やそうとしました。

slashRows.en: The planning team noticed that this would not follow the written guideline if the index reached 35 at one.
slashRows.jp: 計画班は、一時に指数が35になればそれだけでは書かれた指針を守れないと気づきました。

slashRows.en: They moved long-distance running to nine twenty, when the forecast value was still below the extra-break level.
slashRows.jp: 長距離走を、追加休憩基準より低い予報の九時二十分へ移しました。

slashRows.en: The opening program was shortened slightly, so runners still had time to prepare before the earlier race.
slashRows.jp: 開会プログラムを少し短くし、選手が早まった競技の前にも準備時間を取れるようにしました。

slashRows.en: The soccer final was harder to move because both teams also had morning matches.
slashRows.jp: サッカー決勝は両チームに午前試合もあり、時刻移動が難しい競技でした。

slashRows.en: Organizers prepared an indoor skills final in the gym if the one-o'clock measured index reached 35 or above.
slashRows.jp: 一時の実測指数が35以上なら、体育館で屋内技能決勝を行う案を用意しました。

slashRows.en: The gym had enough space for both teams and officials but not for every spectator.
slashRows.jp: 体育館は両チームと役員には十分ですが、全観客は入りませんでした。

slashRows.en: A live screen was placed at the large shaded west entrance so additional spectators could watch from outside the playing area.
slashRows.jp: 追加の観客が競技区域外から見られるよう、大きな日陰の西入口に中継画面を置きました。

slashRows.en: The shade map also showed that Station B in the center field had no nearby cover at midday.
slashRows.jp: 日陰図では中央の給水所Bは正午ごろ近くに日陰がありませんでした。

slashRows.en: A temporary canopy and benches were moved to Station B so students could drink while seated out of direct sun.
slashRows.jp: 直射日光を避け座って飲めるよう、Bへ仮設テントとベンチを移しました。

slashRows.en: Each team received a scheduled water break after every match, and teachers kept a simple record of students using the cool rest room.
slashRows.jp: 各チームは試合後ごとに予定された給水休憩を取り、先生は涼しい休憩室を使った生徒を簡単に記録しました。

slashRows.en: At twelve thirty, the measured index was 34, so low-intensity outdoor activities continued with the added breaks.
slashRows.jp: 十二時半の実測は34だったため、低強度の屋外活動は追加休憩付きで続きました。

slashRows.en: At one, the index reached 35 exactly, so the prepared change for hard outdoor activities was used.
slashRows.jp: 一時にはちょうど35となり、激しい屋外活動について準備した変更を実施しました。

slashRows.en: The soccer final changed to the indoor skills format, while a relay planned for later was moved to a cooler practice day.
slashRows.jp: サッカー決勝は屋内技能形式へ変え、その後のリレーはより涼しい練習日へ移しました。

slashRows.en: Families were told the changes followed the measured index and school guideline.
slashRows.jp: 家庭には、変更が実測指数と学校指針に基づくと伝えました。

slashRows.en: The final report recorded schedule changes, shade, water breaks, and three students who rested for the rest of the event.
slashRows.jp: 最終報告は予定変更、日陰、給水休憩、その後休んだ三人も記録しました。

slashRows.en: The school did not call the day risk-free just because the revised plan worked.
slashRows.jp: 修正版が機能しただけで、学校はその日を危険ゼロとはしませんでした。

slashRows.en: Students learned to combine measured heat, activity level, shade, water, timing, and a change rule.
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちは、実測の暑さ、活動強度、日陰、給水、時刻、変更基準を組み合わせると学びました。

freeWriteTask.prompt: 本文と資料を参考に、暑い日の学校行事を安全に行うための提案を英語20〜30語で書きなさい。
freeWriteTask.modelAnswer: Check the measured heat index before each event, move hard activities to cooler times, and provide shaded water breaks for every team.
